rollups.text: Crystal’s estate-planning timeline: On 2024-03-01 she began listing assets and recorded her home at 45 Coral Bay Rd, valued at $350,000; on 2024-03-15 she described planning gifts for her parents, a care fund, and provisions for her children, and was weighing Douglas versus Kevin as executor. She planned to consult attorney Stephanie on 2024-03-22, held a family meeting with Kimberly and Bradley on 2024-03-25, and faced a 2024-05-15 will deadline. Douglas accepted the executor role on 2024-04-15; Crystal later said she and Douglas finalized the choice after six weeks of consideration. She used WillMaker Pro to prepare and later update a draft, and by 2024-05-02 said it named Douglas executor, Kevin alternate executor, Stephanie guardian for Francis and Michael, Kevin alternate guardian and trustee, and included asset-distribution and funeral instructions; she had not signed it then. She reported updating her will on 2024-08-05 to increase her children’s inheritance by 10%, added guardianship duties on 2024-08-07, and planned legal review with Stephanie. In November 2024 she chose attorney Diana, accepted her $900 fee, and had a stated 2024-12-15 completion deadline. On 2025-02-12 she said her attorney confirmed compliance with 2025 Montserrat regulations and electronic-signature laws; on 2025-02-16 she said she electronically filed the will and the court accepted it, and on 2025-02-20 she reported 100% completion. However, that same day she also said she had never completed or signed will documents with Diana or another attorney, leaving the execution and filing status contradictory and unresolved in the records.

Crystal’s executor decision developed amid disagreement. On 2024-03-15 she was considering Douglas for his organizational skills and Kevin for his legal background; her mother Kimberly preferred Kevin, and Crystal faced an April 1 decision deadline. A 2024-03-25 family meeting included Kimberly and Bradley. On 2024-04-10 Crystal, Douglas, and Kevin disagreed about executor duties during a call but resolved the disagreement by defining the role. Douglas accepted the executor position at Coral Bay Café on 2024-04-15. On 2024-05-02 Crystal remained concerned about her parents’ reaction and decided to arrange another face-to-face family meeting. By 2024-08-10 she said she and Douglas had finalized the choice after six weeks of consideration.

Crystal’s guardianship planning evolved from considering provisions for her children Francis, Michael, and Rachel in March 2024 to a draft naming Stephanie guardian for Francis and Michael by 2024-04-28; on 2024-05-02 she said Kevin would be the alternate and Kevin trustee for a trust for Francis and Michael. In July 2024 Crystal and another party compromised on a $5,000 emergency fund for guardianship expenses; she worried it might be inadequate in August and considered discussing an increase to $10,000 with Douglas. On 2024-08-07 she added guardianship duties including school enrollment and medical decisions, and said she would review them with Stephanie. She later reported a $50,000 allocation on 2025-02-20 and said she had increased the fund to $60,000 that day. The records also show a separate $3,000 life-insurance policy was postponed until 2025, with no confirmation that it was purchased.

Crystal progressively added digital-asset provisions and security measures to her estate planning. On 2024-04-25 she enabled two-factor authentication on all online accounts; on 2024-04-29 she added Vimeo management instructions, and on 2024-04-30 she added Netflix and Spotify provisions. On 2024-05-02 she planned to leave Netflix and Spotify to Francis and Michael and create a secure inventory for Douglas. She added Dropbox backup instructions on 2024-08-06, scheduled a digital-asset review for 2024-09-20, and on 2024-11-05 added Instagram and TikTok legacy provisions valued together at $800. She said she implemented 1Password on 2024-11-07 and helped Natalie test it on 2024-11-09; she felt passwords were synced correctly by 2024-11-12. On 2025-02-01 Rachel began helping with quarterly digital-asset inventories, and Crystal said she would work with Rachel on setup and review beginning 2025-03-01. The records do not confirm all recommended security steps were completed.

Digital assets Crystal specifically mentioned or provided estate instructions for: Adobe Creative Cloud subscription valued at $2,000 (2024-03-15); Netflix, costing $1,200 per year, and Spotify, costing $500 per year, with provisions added 2024-04-30 and intended recipients Francis and Michael discussed 2024-05-02; Vimeo account valued at $3,000, with management instructions added 2024-04-29; Dropbox storage described as worth $1,500, with backup instructions added 2024-08-06; Instagram and TikTok accounts valued together at $800, with digital-legacy provisions added 2024-11-05; cryptocurrency wallets holding $1,000, with transfer instructions reportedly added 2024-11-06. These are the stated values and dates in the records, not independently verified appraisals.

Estate-planning assets Crystal listed or described with values: home at 45 Coral Bay Rd, valued at $350,000 on 2024-03-01 and appraised at $365,000 on 2024-08-04; savings of $25,000, film equipment valued at $15,000, and a 2018 Toyota RAV4 valued at $18,000, listed by 2024-03-15. On 2024-05-02 Crystal said she had kept the film equipment intact while considering whether to sell it to fund a trust. On 2025-02-20 she said her completed estate-planning binder included the deed to her $365,000 home.

Crystal’s estate-tax and gifting planning changed over time. On 2024-03-15 she described a 15% estate-tax rate above $200,000, then asked about a hypothetical 12% rate; the assistant’s calculations and proposed strategies were examples, not adopted plans. A later record says she consulted a tax advisor and adjusted her estimate to 12% above $200,000. On 2024-05-02 she said accountant Christina suggested annual gifts of $15,000 and Crystal planned to verify Montserrat rules and track gifts. In November 2024 she asked about tax thresholds and beneficiary changes; tax figures given by the assistant were not independently verified. On 2025-02-20 Christina advised gifting $15,000 annually to each of Crystal’s three children, totaling $45,000 per year; Crystal asked how to implement this but did not say she had begun gifting.

Crystal’s estate-planning attorney arrangements changed in late 2024. Stephanie had been associated with her estate plan and was expected to retire in March 2025. On 2024-11-08 Crystal chose Diana, citing Diana’s technology expertise rather than Stephanie’s recommended attorney Scott; she accepted Diana’s $900 fee, compared with Scott’s $1,200 retainer. On 2024-11-12 she was trying to finalize her will with Diana before a stated December 15 deadline. Crystal later said on 2025-02-12 that her attorney confirmed compliance with 2025 regulations and electronic-signature laws. Records do not establish the terms of Diana’s services, and one later assistant response confusingly referred to Diana without resolving discrepancies in the earlier attorney history.

Estate-planning education and assessment events Crystal completed: she read “Estate Planning Basics” by Montserrat Legal Aid on 2024-03-05 and rated it 4.5/5; attended an online Montserrat probate-laws seminar on 2024-04-18 and scored 92%; completed the “Guardianship and Minor Care” webinar on 2024-08-02 and scored 88%; attended an “Estate Tax Planning” workshop on 2024-11-02; and completed “Advanced Probate Strategies” on 2025-02-10, scoring 95%.

Crystal’s reported estate-plan completion rose from 75% by 2024-05-01 to about 90% on 2024-08-10, then to 100% on 2025-02-20. The May 2024 75% figure was supplied by the assistant, while the August and February completion figures were reported by Crystal. Her original stated will deadline was 2024-05-15; she later reported completion ahead of that original goal.

Estate-related places and gifts recorded: Crystal’s family meeting with Kimberly and Bradley took place at her home on 2024-03-25; Douglas accepted the executor role at Coral Bay Café on 2024-04-15; Douglas gave Crystal a $500 gift card to The Green Mango restaurant on 2024-04-27; he booked her a surprise three-night stay at Seaside Retreat on 2024-11-11; he planned a surprise dinner at The Blue Lagoon on 2025-02-19; and Stephanie gave Crystal a congratulatory gift basket on 2025-02-17. Crystal scheduled a will-signing ceremony for 2024-12-14 at Montserrat Legal Center, 12 Queen’s Road, although the records do not confirm it occurred.
